issues.body:
## Current REM-001 reconciliation — 2026-09-20

This umbrella remains **open**. Current authority is #79/#80 and
`docs/operations/development-claims-remediation-programme.md` (PR #88).

- #9 remains closed as scoped characterization evidence; it is not broad gameplay acceptance.
- #10 is reopened as the player/granular evidence-objective anchor. Its bounded policy/fixture evidence is retained, while #82 owns current broad player/granular remediation and owner acceptance.
- #11 is reopened as the body/granular evidence-objective anchor. Its bounded 2026-09-13 repair evidence is retained; #81 owns reconstruction/integration into current main and #83 owns broad body/granular acceptance after #81.
- #12 remains independently open as the scalable-soliding programme. Stage 3B is active and is **not** the sole remaining reason #8 is open.

Do not start duplicate implementation work under #10 or #11; use #82 and #81/#83 respectively. Historical comments/checkpoints remain evidence of the repository state when they were written.

---

Improve granular material interactions and barrel support, then investigate reversible soliding for Rapier macro-object motion and ballistics.

## Intended behaviour

- Settled solids/powders should not pass through each other solely because of density.
- Support-capable powders should interact consistently with the player.
- Dense liquids should not freely cross packed powders. Mercury may retain much slower penetration.
- The red test rectangles are called **barrels**. Ordinary impacts should embed them by no more than roughly half their depth, then stop further sinking.
- Rested, mostly contiguous same-material regions may eventually use reversible aggregate representations for Rapier positioning and ballistics, while loose piles must remain able to collapse.

## Historical delivery sequence — superseded by REM-001 on 2026-09-20

- [ ] #9 — Characterisation fixtures, bounded telemetry and a measured baseline; ready to start.
- [ ] #10 — Powder/player support and controlled material exchange; depends on #9.
- [ ] #11 — Barrel embedding and persistent granular support; depends on #9 and the shared support policy in #10.
- [ ] #12 — Reversible soliding design and bounded prototype; informed by #9, support integration depends on #10/#11, and dynamic aggregates require an ownership ADR.

Each work issue links back here and carries its own acceptance checklist. This parent closes only when all four agreed deliverables have evidence or an explicit recorded scope decision.

## Shared constraints

Use the [physics characterisation plan](https://github.com/techrote/cybersand/blob/ab4851e/docs/operations/physics-characterisation-plan.md) as the detailed experiment specification. Its 2026-09-08 diagnosis is source inspection, not new runtime acceptance; inspect actual HEAD and rebuilt artifacts before testing. Numerical sweeps, Mercury slowdown ratios, timing windows and one-cell tolerances are provisional. Preserve the owner's roughly half-depth requirement while finalising its ordinary-impact envelope from measurements.

Preserve native material authority, main-thread Rapier ownership, immutable handoffs, bounded work/capacity outcomes, conservation and the failed-tick/interest-region contracts covered by #1 and #2. Do not introduce per-cell physics bodies or erase/simulate/restore as the collision representation. Desktop async, native/fallback and real Web profiles require distinct evidence.

Keep implementation, diagnostics and raw logs in the active development workspace; update canonical documentation, tests and dated source/artifact evidence at each checkpoint.

issues.title: Physics: support the player on powders and control granular/liquid exchange
issues.body:
## REM-001 current status — 2026-09-20

**Reopened for truthful broad-objective tracking; historical bounded evidence is not retracted.**

The 2026-09-09 versioned player/support and liquid/powder policy checkpoint remains valid within its recorded fixtures, source/artifacts and platform limits. Later owner gameplay evaluation found the broader player/granular interaction materially below acceptable, so `closed/completed` no longer represents the original broad objective.

#82 / REM-003 is the **only active implementation/remediation lane** for current broad player/granular behaviour. Do not create a second #10 implementation branch. This issue is now the evidence/objective anchor and remains open until #82 supplies explicit owner acceptance or an allowed evidence-backed disposition.

Authority: #79, #80, PR #88, and `docs/operations/development-claims-remediation-programme.md`.

---

Parent: #8. **Depends on #9** for baseline measurements and final acceptance values.

## Resulting behaviour

Settled support-capable powders should support the player and resist density-only interpenetration. Grains must still fall through real voids and avalanche. Dense liquids must follow an explicit liquid/powder permeability policy; Mercury may retain visibly much slower penetration.

The plan's source inspection found hard-surface-or-Sand player predicates and density exchange without a powder/powder exclusion. Mercury's downward exchange occurs before the lateral viscosity gate. Confirm the actual paths against #9 before implementation.

## Work

- Specify a shared, material-aware support policy that separates settled packing/support from density and hard-surface identity. Define downward support and side resistance independently so airborne Dust does not become an invisible wall.
- Separate movement into Empty, powder/powder rearrangement and liquid/powder exchange. Define allowed pairs, support/yield conditions and independent permeability rates.
- Cover all eligible downward/diagonal swap paths and either initiator; avoid alternate move attempts multiplying a configured rate.
- Add bounded deterministic eligibility/wake scheduling for slow Mercury exchange. Sleeping blocks must still eventually progress; excluded regions must not accrue catch-up motion.
- Update native and sampled-player/fallback paths deliberately, recording any retained semantic differences.
- Land player/support policy and exchange rules as separate focused changes with shared regression fixtures.

## Provisional experiments

Use #9 to finalise the numbers. Screen Mercury exchange at one opportunity per 10/30/60 ticks or an equivalent time-scaled rate, and local support occupancy at 0.65/0.8/0.95 in a specified bounded neighbourhood. The plan's 10–50× slower Mercury front speed in packed Sand is a proposed target, not an already accepted constant. Keep density meaningful; increasing viscosity alone cannot gate downward exchange, and a global target-side exchange prohibition also changes gas/liquid displacement.

## Acceptance

- [ ] P1: packed resting powder pairs do not reorder solely due to density; void falling, slopes, Stone modes and collapse remain meaningful.
- [ ] P2: Mercury penetrates the canonical packed bed much more slowly while making measurable progress; other liquid/powder pair policies are explicit and tested in both layer orders.
- [ ] P3: support-capable powders stop ordinary player downward passage, with standing/walking/landing, slopes, side approach, loose grains and enclosed-spawn coverage.
- [ ] P5/P6: excavation removes support; delayed interactions survive sleep/wake; region exclusion/re-entry preserves #1/#2 contracts.
- [ ] No silent material loss; Water mass and reaction accounting remain correct. Preserve fast Water fronts/spray/film and established material feel.
- [ ] Matching-configuration repeat/worker parity, bounded work/capacity, source-matched desktop and affected real Web profiles have scoped evidence.
- [ ] Update material/coupling/player policy, configuration, tests, roadmap and retrieval documentation; proposed fixture values become runtime settings only through an explicit versioned configuration decision.

Detailed scope and tuning: [physics characterisation plan](https://github.com/techrote/cybersand/blob/ab4851e/docs/operations/physics-characterisation-plan.md#phase-3-parameter-experiments-then-model-changes).

issues.body:
## Owner / generic-body clarification — 2026-09-20

The red "barrel" is a deliberately simple **generic rectangular Rapier reference body**, not a special gameplay object or a separate support subsystem. The owner does **not** recall accepting the historical #11 barrel-support result as final behavior.

The 2026-09-13 branch/evidence therefore remains useful **bounded historical implementation evidence**, including the recorded masked-source/ejection/bearing improvements, but it must not be cited as owner acceptance of finished body physics.

#81 remains the remediation/provenance owner for reconstructing what happened to those bounded semantics on current main. It must reconcile only still-valid **generic body↔cellular** semantics and must not install a barrel-only path. The WEX programme (#90), #91 generic Rapier↔Water baseline and later #92 hybrid proof are complementary generic-coupling evidence; live #12 ownership must be checked before overlapping implementation.

This issue remains an evidence/objective anchor, not a duplicate implementation lane.

---

## REM-001 current status — 2026-09-20

**Reopened for truthful integration/broad-objective tracking; historical bounded evidence is not retracted.**

The source-matched 2026-09-13 repair remains valid for its documented ordinary rectangle/load envelope. Its evidence commit is `d5f0de687283ec366ed4ff33160a274e2a35ddc6` and the accepted code/runtime checkpoint recorded there is `f8720d331e653ff40c12149dc1b7164724accd9f`. Audited current main `e87ac54459a3a62350fa7aa3da6ce979c30a18b8` does **not** contain that accepted bearing/masked-source/bounded-ejection implementation.

#81 / REM-002 is the **only active lane** for reconstructing/reconciling that bounded accepted repair into current main. After #81, #83 / REM-004 owns the broader body/granular gameplay envelope and explicit owner acceptance. Do not create a duplicate #11 implementation branch.

Authority: #79, #80, PR #88, and `docs/operations/development-claims-remediation-programme.md`.

---

Parent: #8. **Depends on #9 and the shared support policy in #10.**

## Problem and intended behaviour

The red test rectangles are **barrels**. They currently continue sinking through Sand/powders. Ordinary impacts should embed them by no more than roughly half their depth, then remain supported. Support must disappear when the bed is excavated or collapses.

The planning inspection found displacement/contact/pressure impulses with a per-tick cap, density clamping and stale-sample attenuation, but no persistent granular bearing model. Use #9 to establish which terms and timing effects explain the observed trajectories.

## Work

- Compare existing impulse terms one family at a time using #9 telemetry. Measure per-face cancellation, cap saturation, unresolved overlap and accepted impulse age.
- Prototype material/packing-aware static support, depth/compaction-dependent yield and velocity-dependent penetration resistance. Define units and timestep scaling before calibrating load-bearing.
- Give each contact mode one solver owner. Do not add both a Rapier support collider and cellular support impulses for the same load.
- Use actual bed support; a fixed world-height clamp or permanent freezing would fail excavation/collapse requirements.
- Preserve separate liquid behaviour and existing hard-terrain/CCD handling. Treat fast/thin/rotating body failures independently of ordinary static support.

## Measurement and provisional gate

For an initially flat bed and downward-positive coordinates, record depth relative to the **pre-impact** surface: max(0, bottom_y - initial_surface_y). Also record local deformed-surface depth, crater shape and rotation. For a rotated rectangle, projected vertical extent H = abs(cos(theta))*height + abs(sin(theta))*width. Place the hard floor well below the embed region so it cannot masquerade as granular support.

The owner's requirement is roughly half-depth followed by stability. The plan proposes peak/final depth no greater than 0.5 H + 1 cell, and at most one cell of further descent in the last ten seconds of a 30-second run, followed by a 120-second creep check. Finalise tolerance/timing from #9 before claiming acceptance.

Start with the 8×14, mass-1 barrel and drops from one and four body heights. Gentle placement can stay shallow. Eight-body-height impacts, thin/unsupported beds, alternate masses and larger/rotated bodies expand the stress envelope rather than silently redefining ordinary acceptance.

## Acceptance

- [ ] P4 ordinary impacts meet the documented half-depth/stability envelope on Sand and representative powders; publish peak/final depth and long-duration creep plots.
- [ ] P5 excavation and loss of support cause appropriate motion, without hovering or stale collider trapping.
- [ ] Test mass 0.5/1/2, upright/45°/sideways, size variants, slopes and multiple barrels; report the supported-load envelope and stress-case limits.
- [ ] Liquid and hard-floor controls retain distinct behaviour, with conservation and unresolved overlap reported.
- [ ] Document sample-age/latency sensitivity; validate desktop async and affected real Web profiles, including seams and sleep/re-entry.
- [ ] Bound telemetry, support/contact work and shape capacity; preserve #1/#2 regressions and applicable worker parity.
- [ ] Update coupling, support ownership, units/configuration, tests and dated evidence. Any new torque/CCD/substep scope has explicit numerical and work budgets.

Candidate sweeps for gains, caps, damping, friction, latency and support response are in the [physics characterisation plan](https://github.com/techrote/cybersand/blob/ab4851e/docs/operations/physics-characterisation-plan.md#phase-3-parameter-experiments-then-model-changes). They are provisional, not production defaults.

all four complete conversations, later refinements, rejected alternatives and
repository conflicts. It is the traceability record; this page owns the programme.
Future implementers use the linked prompts without needing those conversations.

## A. Current relevant architecture and accepted decisions

Intake is local `8f4ffb96e03dc50cb43ab9c84de17ccb44c03774` in
`C:/kybersand/source`. The existing rebuilt Windows DLL is deliberately dirty;
its identity is in the ledger. Remote main is older. Source changes and runtime
evidence from #9/#10/#13 plus September 10 Water work are local baseline inputs,
not silently certified by GitHub issue closure or a profile hash.

| Authority | Relevant baseline |
|---|---|
| CURRENT / VALIDATED within dated fixtures | Native `World::Chunk::Cell` is 4 bytes: 8-bit material, state_a, state_b, updated_epoch. Material state is typed by each material's behavior; temperature is optional persistent chunk SoA state. |
| ACCEPTED / ADR-001/003/007/009 | Native owns material; Rapier owns independent bodies on the main thread. Packed values cross owner boundaries. Separate transient body-ID occupancy is stable during cellular work. Retained immutable render payloads never expose mutable cells. |
| CURRENT with known limitations | Rectangle coupling accepts at most 16 bodies, bounded sweep/ejection, capped central impulses and stale-sample handling. Failed ejection retains material and reports overlap. #9 documents masked-source feedback and barrier-crossing ejection; this programme does not assume #11 fixed them. |
| ACCEPTED / ADR-002/004/010 | Phased in-place four-phase worker execution; excluded regions pause without catch-up. A failed World is quarantined until reset/replacement; no global transaction/automatic retry. Buffered is not executable rollback. |
| ACCEPTED / ADR-005; CURRENT POLICY | FreeMass Water has exact closed-operation integer conservation and stable equilibrium. Current lateral request is floor(3*imbalance/4), with one-unit tolerance, gravity first, 12-tick coherent delay and supported film at mass <=48/255. |
| CURRENT | Water alone has fractional quantity. Other liquids use whole-cell paths, generally CellularYield; Oil has specialized movement. A mobility roll and scheduler sleep are not an explicit stress/yield model. No generic persistent cellular vx/vy exists. |
| CURRENT POLICY / ADR-011 and #13 | Powder density sorting is excluded, player packing/support is separate, Mercury permeability defaults to period 30. Motion-driven mixing/carrying is opt-in; gameplay Baseline remains disabled. Horizontal candidates 2 and cadence 1 are protected defaults. |
| ACCEPTED / ADR-008 | Explicit bounded approximation does not waive occupancy, ownership, capacity or current conservation contracts. New approximation needs its own measured policy. |

Storage chunk 128², activity block 32², scheduling core 64², and radius-two
expanded write domain 68² are independent units. At 4/8 bytes their cell-only
payloads are respectively 64/128 KiB, 4/8 KiB, 16/32 KiB, and
18.0625/36.125 KiB. These exclude temperature, occupancy, metadata, stacks,
snapshots and allocator overhead and are **not measured cache conclusions**.
Current ordinary liquid writes remain adjacent; transport hooks may reach radius
two. A 64² hard-terrain collider packet is yet another unit.

## B. Decision ledger and authority rules

Use these statuses claim by claim, not one label for a whole workstream:

| Status | Meaning here |
|---|---|
| CURRENT / VALIDATED | Implemented and supported by identified retained evidence, only in its measured scope. |
| CURRENT POLICY | Deliberately selected versioned tuning/behavior; changing it requires new evidence and a policy decision. |
| ACCEPTED / ADR | Explicit architectural authority; experiments cannot silently supersede it. |
| ISSUE-SCOPED | Temporary restriction belonging to an issue, such as #13's no general velocity field. |
| EXPERIMENT | Candidate requiring controlled measurement. |
| OPEN | Unresolved question or insufficient evidence. |
| SUPERSEDED | Earlier claim or preference displaced by identified later reasoning/source. |
| REJECTED | Explicitly declined hypothesis/design, with its rejection scope preserved. |
| DEFERRED | Deliberately postponed, not rejected or already implemented. |

Key dispositions: retain ADR-007; do not place occupancy in persistent Cell.
Conservation flexibility from W is an OPEN proposed revision, not a revoked
ADR-005. Compact history is an EXPERIMENT; neither universally required nor
permanently prohibited. W's bottom-fill-everywhere suggestion is SUPERSEDED by
local oriented reconstruction; its early preference for only transient direction
is refined by the final request to test persistent material-local memory.
I's four-byte preference and D0–D5 sequence remain proposals, constrained by the
later width/state experiments. Native coherent bodies belong to existing #12,
not Current architecture. Fracture/torque/anchors/rebaking stay DEFERRED.

The detailed ledger also resolves two easy misreadings: state_b is Water's
coherence countdown, not a universal calm/stability field; and the source's
epoch-zero reservation makes repeated wrap clears 255 ticks apart, or 63 for
an otherwise comparable 6-bit design, after the first clear at 256/64.

### May extra Cell bits hold occupancy or relax exact Water conservation?

No. **ACCEPTED ADR-007** keeps transient rigid-body occupancy separate from
persistent material state, regardless of spare bits. **ACCEPTED ADR-005** retains
exact closed Water conservation. The programme can investigate deliberately
bounded numerical error only where a candidate demonstrates a reason to need it,
with an exact control, explicit error ledger and later architecture decision.
No experiment silently amends either ADR; shared or missing material ownership
is never numerical approximation.

### Does closed issue #11 prove barrel support is ready for soliding?

No. GitHub marks #11 closed, but the intake source and retained evidence still
describe missing persistent barrel bearing, masked-source feedback and
barrier-crossing ejection. Soliding issue #12 can begin bounded diagnostics and
design; support-dependent integration requires a source-matched fix and evidence
or an explicit scope decision. Administrative issue closure is not runtime
acceptance. The programme records this conflict without reopening or replacing
the owner's issue.

## C. Questions and bounded outcomes

| Key | One meaningful outcome | Live question / why it exists |
|---|---|---|
| C — Liquid characterization | Evidence map and minimum missing measurements for present FreeMass/CellularYield | Which observed behavior belongs to quantity, transport, mobility, special rules or sleep, and which merits changing? |
| L — Layout and epoch cost | Controlled cost/compatibility comparison of current, padded, packed and sidecar layouts | What does raw width cost; what do masks/accessors and epoch frequency add; what state/ID capacity is actually justified? |
| P — State precision | Quantity/auxiliary precision response curves at fixed layout and algorithm | What do 4/6/8/10-bit mass and separately packed delay buy or lose, including active lifetime and films? |
| M — Compact motion | Controlled no-history versus local flow-memory comparison, inline versus sidecar | Can a small decaying direction/strength field improve a named jet/spray deficit with bounded local writes, and at what cost? |
| V — Fractional presentation | Oriented fractional-interface visual/cost comparison on frozen authoritative states | Can existing mass information improve surfaces, underfaces, edges and droplets without new simulation state? |
| B — Conditional sparse motion | Small bounded ballistic promotion/demotion feasibility result, or documented no-go | Is high-speed/event motion still worth a distinct representation after compact-history evidence and transfer design? |
| G — Decision record | Cross-workstream evidence review, retained-baseline or selected next increment | Which measured combination warrants a scoped follow-up and what must remain open? This does not itself implement migration. |

Existing **#12** remains the coherent-body/soliding research owner. This programme
provides a self-contained execution supplement, not a duplicate aggregate issue.
Its diagnostics/design can proceed from existing #9 evidence. Support integration
still requires verified support evidence, including resolution of the closed-#11
conflict. Dynamic membership requires an explicit reviewed ownership ADR first.
A near-rest restricted prototype does not need B if it can state its momentum
limits honestly; energetic reversal must wait for a selected motion representation.

## D. Candidate matrix and controlled variables

| Question | Baseline / candidates | Change versus fixed controls | Required measurement |
|---|---|---|---|
| Raw Cell width | Current 4 B; 8 B with four original bytes and four unused bytes | Change stride only. Same semantics, epoch width, geometry, traversal, input, descriptors and compact snapshots. Verify compiler actually emits an 8-byte stride. | Equal content/events/work; tick distribution, ns/visited cell, memory/traffic, worker scaling. |
| Packed access | Packed 8/16/8 control; 16/40/8 with only legacy state used; padded 8 B control | Access arrangement/ID extraction; fixed semantic values, epoch and unused capacity. | Masks/read-modify-write cost, size/alignment, no truncation, generated access path, normalized semantic equality. |
| Short epoch | Packed 8/16/8 versus 8/18/6, extra two state bits unused | Epoch width/clear period only after access cost is known. | Per-clear duration and exact ticks, p99/max, double-update prevention over wraps/sleep/re-entry. |
| Optional state allocation | 4 B plus chunk/block SoA or bounded sparse indexed sidecar versus 8 B inline | First legacy-equivalent storage/access; later identical M semantics and state precision. Same populated positions, lifetimes and work policy. | Zero/1/5/15/50/100% use, clustered versus dispersed use, lookup/move/reclaim cost, total bytes incl metadata and saturated capacity. |
| Material ID headroom | Current 8-bit IDs; 10-bit 10/14/8 alternative; 16-bit candidate | Access cost separated from catalogue expansion. 10/14/8 cannot be a full legacy control unless every material's state is losslessly representable. | Actual catalogue/ID needs and adapter/render/profile/save migration surface. No new material pack loader. |
| Water mass | 8-bit reference; 4/6/10; 3/12 optional only to locate an observed failure boundary | Fixed tested layout, three-quarter local solver, mass-normalized thresholds, no history. Auxiliary delay remains 12 ticks. | Initial quantization ledger, exact integer mass per precision, normalized levelness/front/rest/film, work and timing. |
| Auxiliary precision | Original 8-bit Water delay versus 4-bit representation | Only packing; same 0..12 countdown, max-on-merge, pre-decrement suppression. Other materials retain their own full state range. | Exact behavioral equality and bit access cost. Combined budgets only after isolated results. |
| Yield versus sleeping | Actual Water and representative yield liquids; default quiet threshold 3 versus threshold exceeding fixture horizon | Change sleep diagnostic only; same liquid, viscosity, scene and input. Zero is invalid, not a sleep-disable option. | Late mobility failures, eligible attempts, active-block time, residual slope and wake response. |
| Flow memory | No history versus small direction/strength/age; inline versus sidecar | First fixed mass precision, solver and layout; next same memory semantics across storage. No new pressure/velocity solver. | Jet COM/range/asymmetry, split/merge/decay accounting, rest, active lifetime, CPU/memory. |
| Presentation | Current stable dither/binary view; fractional coverage; local-gradient oriented interface | Same frozen mass frames and simulation inputs. Optional render flux only as separately measured second stage. | Area error, seam/orientation artifacts, temporal flicker, CPU/snapshot/upload/GPU cost. |
| Sparse motion | Selected local/history control; bounded native pool with position/velocity/material/state | Matched event input, mass and environment. New representation explicitly changes semantics, never labeled a layout benchmark. | Trajectory/range, swept barrier contact, singular owner, refused reinsertion, conservation, peak pool/queue/scratch and time. |

No full Cartesian product is required. Screen isolated variables, reject dominated
or unsafe candidates, then compare only interactions whose independent results
justify them. No 16/32-byte universal baseline, full velocity field, broad liquid
unification or geometry resize is created merely because it appeared in discussion.

## E. Cross-workstream dependency and conflict matrix

| Cross-link | Constraint / evidence flow |
|---|---|
| L → P/M and P/M → L | Measure representation tax before spending capacity; measured useful state then tells whether universal width or sparse state pays. A raw benchmark does not select a solver. |
| L ↔ geometry | Keep 128/32/64/radius-2 fixed for width screen. A 64² storage-chunk experiment is a separate registered interaction only if cache evidence warrants it; never quietly shrink scheduling cores or halos. |
| C → P/M/V | Reuse measured fronts/rest/films and attribute special cases before testing precision/history/reconstruction. Retained #9/#13 are not complete sleep/precision studies. |
| Quantity ↔ algorithm | Partial quantity does not mandate equalization; equalization does not justify all liquids becoming fractional. Generalization needs unlike-liquid capacity, density and reaction source/sink contracts. |
| C/P/M ↔ #10/#13 policy | Keep Mercury period 30, powder/player policy and protected profile defaults. Compare intentional Water/mixing deltas separately from regressions; changed flux can change pickup without any profile change. |
| Occupancy ↔ L/M/B/#12 | Derived body mask remains outside Cell. Adding bits changes neither Rapier ownership nor material authority. Body/event velocity is a possible motion source, not generic cell state. |
| M ↔ B | Local decaying memory can address directional persistence without continuous coordinates; high-speed travel may still need sparse promotion. Neither evidence result logically settles the other requirement. |
| B ↔ L | Sparse motion may avoid ubiquitous state but adds pools/lookups/transfer cost; wider cells may simplify state transfer but do not provide continuous trajectories. Measure density crossover. |
| #12 ↔ B/M | Energetic demotion needs an explicit motion carrier; near-rest restriction may avoid it. Preserve payload/mass/temperature and parent v + omega cross r if inheriting rigid motion. |
| #12 ↔ coupling/terrain | Terrain collider removal, dynamic activation and endpoint mask installation need acknowledged topology handover; ordinary aged transform samples cannot authorize it. |
| V ↔ P/M | Rendering may use existing normalized mass; it does not block on wider cells or motion adoption. Only after M shows useful history should V test exposing a narrow derived field. |
| Error policy ↔ every transfer | Exact current Water oracle stays intact. Candidate drift must have explicit numerical budget and benefit; ownership loss/duplication is never classified as numerical approximation. |

## F. Regression baselines and retained evidence

Use the ledger's checkpoint table (`architecture-programme-source-ledger.md#repository-intake-and-evidence-reuse` in the local planning checkout)
and the canonical physics runbook (`physics-characterisation.md` in the local planning checkout). Do not commission
another #9 audit. C first extracts existing results; it instruments/runs only
unanswered cases. New candidates later require focused source-matched comparisons.

| Baseline / actual touchpoints | Required preservation or explicit delta |
|---|---|
| `native/tests/test_world.cpp`: conserved_water_levels_and_sleeps, water_surface_column_mass_is_level, water_conserves_across_storage_boundaries, water_lateral_front_and_leveling_speed | Exact closed integer totals, stable content after rest, current front/level bounds, signed seams and one/four-worker parity. Use content_hash for rest, not advancing state_hash. |
| `native/bench/water_leveling.cpp`, `tools/physics/water_leveling.py`, September 10 audit | Current three-quarter and historical half controls are distinct. Reuse 48/96-wide, shifted/mirrored basins; initial 97,920 mass is that fixture, not a universal constant. |
| `native/bench/transport_characterisation.cpp`, `tools/physics/issue13.py`, transport_matrix/report/knobs/permeability | Baseline/Gentle/Erosion, sustained/sparse release, films/barriers, successful-motion counts and Mercury packed/poured/powder references. Do not replay known erroneous injector/erosion-depth measurements. |
| `native/bench/physics_characterisation.cpp`, `godot/tests/test_physics_characterisation.gd`, `tools/physics/water-accounting.json` | Stored material versus masked proxy, crop outflow versus world loss, contact saturation, barrier-aware ejection failure as known control. |
| `godot/tests/test_interaction_policy.gd`, `test_interaction_async.gd`, `test_transport_probe.gd` | Player support, real void collapse, indirect Mercury changes and distinct desktop/native Web/fallback scope. |
| Native failure/region fixtures and `godot/tests/test_render_patch_handoff_regression.gd` | Quarantine, no partial success publication, exclusion/re-entry, immutable delayed-consumer payloads, no catch-up. |

Water films/spray and state/temperature preservation already have tests; use
their existing fixture bodies. New scenarios are limited to missing sleep
isolation, precision error, epoch-tail/sidecar density, directional jets,
oriented frozen frames and bounded promotion failure cases. Serial and fallback
are alternate semantics; do not require their bytes to match phased native.
Native/Wasm current state hashes include platform-width fields; compare normalized
semantic records across ABI rather than claiming cross-ABI full-hash equality.

## G. Measurement protocol

Before candidate implementation, commit a small experiment registration: question,
variants, semantic comparator, selected seeds/scenes, physical units, fixed knobs,
run horizon, capacity limits, instrumentation cost check, primary metric and gate.
Use fresh worlds and pinned release builds. Record source HEAD plus delta,
compiler/flags, CPU/OS, artifact/profile hashes, worker count and exact commands.
Do not measure while other builds run. Keep raw logs in
`C:/kybersand/validation/local/<dated-experiment>/`; retain compact tables and
interpretation under source documentation. Missing PMU/GPU counters are named
gaps, never estimated misses presented as measurements.

Default bounded screen: 5 deterministic seed/translation cases, 1 and 4 workers,
1,800 fixed ticks for behavior; epoch tests at least 2,048 ticks with sleepers
and retained inactive chunks. Performance uses 7 interleaved baseline/candidate
process pairs after a declared 120-tick warmup in the steady workload; startup
and initial settling are measured separately. Registration can reduce redundant
cases using retained evidence, with reasons recorded before candidate results.
Finalists use up to 20 seeds/7,200 ticks only for a specific unresolved long-tail
or drift concern, not an automatic broad campaign.

**Performance:** p50/p95/p99/max microseconds per completed tick and total cost;
ns/visited cell; processed/visited distinction; aggregate active blocks and actual
visited-cell ticks (do not relabel blocks*1024 as exact active cells); successful
transfers/writes/lateral probes; scheduled cores and worker scaling; wake/sleep
churn; epoch clear duration/frequency; cell/sidecar/metadata/snapshot bytes and
total process memory; preparation versus worker allocation, pool high-water and
overflow; stage times/cache/bandwidth where instrumented. Separate render upload,
coupling and full frame pacing from core tick timing.

**Behavior:** exact material ledger and explicit reaction/ROI source/sinks;
normalized Water column-mass spread and levelness; front/discharge/spread;
content-stable time and residual work; supported-film lifetime and tiny residues;
jet range/COM/direction persistence; spray size distribution; species interface
mixing/transport/deposition; penetration/barrier/overlap results; repeat/parity;
render coverage error and temporal artifacts. For B/#12 account for material in
cells, promoted pool/membership, retained pending owner and explicit outputs.
Record momentum separately from intentionally decaying bias.

Research screening defaults (new programme proposals, not existing physics policy):
flag >15% paired p95 core cost regression, >1 ms additional epoch-clear excess
over neighboring ordinary ticks, or unbounded active lifetime for explicit review.
For M/B register a concrete target such as directional COM displacement/range
and a minimum useful improvement before runs; there is no evidence-backed universal
jet-distance target yet. If no target can be justified, return no-go at admission.
Report paired distributions/ranges and measurement noise, not just one percentage.
These flags do not prove a candidate unacceptable for every feature; G compares
benefit and whole cost. A changed budget is a new registered experiment, not a
post-hoc waiver. No production migration is authorized by passing these screens.

## H. Dependency graph

Logical keys were defined before new issue numbers. Solid prerequisites consume
evidence; conditional branches must have a recorded admission or no-go outcome.

```text
Current source + retained ADR/#9/#10/#13/Water evidence
          |                              |
          v                              v
 C: characterize missing facts     L: isolate layout/packing/epoch cost
          | evidence                     | evidence
          v                              v
 G-C: admit a behavior question     G-L: valid equivalent-semantics comparison
          |                   \          /
          |                    v        v
          |                   P: precision / auxiliary allocation
          |                              | evidence -> G-P
          v                              v
 V: frozen-frame presentation      M: local memory, inline vs sidecar
          |                              | evidence -> G-M
          |                              v
          |                        G-B admission: unmet motion requirement?
          |                          | yes                  | no
          |                          v                      v
          |                     B: bounded proof       recorded no-go
          |                          | evidence              |
          +--------------------------+-----------------------+
                                     v
                         G: architecture decision record
                         /             |                 \
               retain baseline    bounded next test     selected migration
               or defer           with new charter     separately scoped later

 Existing coherent-body research:
 retained evidence -> #12 candidate/design stage -> ownership ADR gate
                     -> conditional near-rest prototype
 support integration requires verified support evidence (#11 conflict resolved)
 energetic reversal requires selected M/B transfer capability, not a ladder
```

V uses C's documented mass/presentation cases and can run alongside L/P.
M waits for L/P to avoid spending unknown capacity. B initially owns only
admission/transfer design; code is conditional on G-B. G is one decision issue
with staged gate entries; its final disposition waits for every admitted branch
or explicit no-go/defer record. #12 is linked context, not a required finish
before a Cell/liquid decision, and does not block C/L/P/V.

## I. Decision gates and conditional work

| Gate | Evidence required | Allowed next step / negative branch |
|---|---|---|
| G-C | Extracted #9/#10/#13/current evidence, exact specialization map, missing sleep/film/flow answers, identified behavior target | Admit P/M/V. Retain separate liquids if no demonstrated need. Quantity/transport generalization or genuine yielding gets a narrowly chartered later issue only for a specific gap. |
| G-L | Semantic equality for stride/access comparisons; epoch differences isolated; wrap safety; full memory and hardware scope | Use candidate layouts as experimental controls. Reject broken packing, retain alternatives; no layout adoption. |
| G-P | Exact per-precision accounting, normalized versus one-unit-threshold separation, retained delay and non-Water range safety | Select state budgets for M or retain 8-bit mass. If precision effects are ambiguous, M uses reference precision. |
| G-M | Named useful motion gain, bounded decay to stable equilibrium, split/merge semantics, cost and storage-density crossover | Retain no history, test viable memory, or admit a distinct high-speed B question. Quantized vx/vy is a later experiment only if cheap memory cannot meet a defined need. |
| G-B | Specific high-speed/body-event use case; comparison versus M/current path; reviewed singular-owner transfer charter; predeclared pool/collision/reinsertion limits | Execute small proof or close B with no-go. No automatic conversion of all failed ejections; no new body system required. |
| G-R for existing #12 | Verified support prerequisite where needed; reviewed ownership ADR; retained source state until capacity/geometry/terrain readiness acknowledgement | One coherent island/one barrel near-rest proof. On failure or missing support evidence remain in design/diagnostics; no deletion or self-collision gap. |
| G-final | Comparable L/P/M/V plus B evidence or no-go, relevant #12 findings, policy/compatibility/platform impacts, remaining uncertainties | Publish retain/defer/next-test/conditional-migration decision. Create a separate production migration issue only with a selected candidate, full prompt, ADR delta and compatibility plan. |

If generalizing FreeMass is admitted later, first specify quantity transactions:
partial unlike liquids sharing/replacing cells, density interpretation, reactions,
product amounts, displacement, films, ledger units and source/sinks. Test one
nonreactive analogue before reactive liquids. If testing genuine yield, vary
yield eligibility independently from lateral mobility and scheduler sleep;
retain current Paste/Slush as controls. Neither branch requires unification.

If an alternative needs numerical drift, register mass error (absolute/relative,
per-operation and accumulated), horizon and benefit before code. Preserve an exact
control and distinguish explicit pruning from rounding and from bugs. ADR-005/008
may only change via an explicit decision; extra state alone is no reason to relax
conservation. These are conditional extensions, not uncreated mandatory backlog.

## J. Integration gates

Changing Current policy requires a separate reviewed decision with scenario-based
benefit, honest negative evidence, representational total cost, supported target
hardware and preserved invariants. Required affected-platform coverage is native
core, desktop asynchronous owner and real Web compatibility/threaded profiles;
document fallback scope deliberately. Check snapshot lifetime and bounded queues
where interfaces change. No visual-only win can waive conservation or ownership.
No raw timing result revises ADRs. Missing target-device/performance evidence
means experimental status, even if native correctness passes.

Any selected ID/state layout migration must inventory C ABI, adapter packets,
material tables, 81-entry profiles/pair matrices, RG8 ID encoding, palette lookup,
hash schema and CYSD1 compatibility. Preserve existing saves or introduce a
versioned converter with explicit refusal of unsupported states. Do not serialize
compiler struct bytes or claim complete replay. Narrow render-derived snapshots
can remain independent of simulation width; 16-bit IDs still need an explicit
render encoding decision before deployment.

For B/#12: define owner before/during/after transfer, state/quantity/temperature,
identity/generation, motion units/inheritance, deterministic order, capacity,
collision/overlap, failure/deferral/cancel/retry, region exit/re-entry and the
chosen save/load boundary. Preflight and reserve destinations before removing
source authority. Reservation is not dual ownership. Do not infer global rollback
from a local transition protocol. Failed ticks continue to use ADR-010 quarantine.

## K. Baseline, rollback and comparison strategy

Keep intake source and each experiment as recoverable commits/branches, with
reference fixtures and full registered input identity. Build candidates separately;
never overwrite the only reference executable or the owner's loaded DLL. Preserve
the intentional dirty DLL and all unrelated work. Raw outputs stay in the active
workspace; `C:/cybersand` remains the functional-deliverables directory.

Use fresh-world A/B selection or distinct binaries, not unsafe live state-layout
switching. Normalize layout-specific state into semantic records for comparison;
epoch-shortening variants intentionally differ in raw bookkeeping but must retain
equivalent material behavior. Keep observer-off controls so instrumentation cannot
silently become the improvement. Preserve failed and ambiguous runs. If a candidate
loses, retain the control and close its experiment with the evidence; do not
generate a migration by momentum. Serial, fallback and unavailable Buffered are
not interchangeable exact rollback implementations.

## Issue and prompt index

The programme above was written before creation. The index records actual
GitHub issues and locally durable prompts after a second overlap check.

| Key | Issue | Self-contained prompt |
|---|---|---|
| C | [#15: Architecture experiment: characterize FreeMass and CellularYield from retained evidence](https://github.com/techrote/cybersand/issues/15) | Liquid characterization (`architecture-programme-prompts/liquid-characterization.md` in the local planning checkout) |
| L | [#16: Architecture experiment: isolate Cell layout, packing, sidecar and epoch costs](https://github.com/techrote/cybersand/issues/16) | Layout and epoch (`architecture-programme-prompts/cell-layout.md` in the local planning checkout) |
| P | [#17: Architecture experiment: measure liquid state precision at fixed layout and semantics](https://github.com/techrote/cybersand/issues/17) | State precision (`architecture-programme-prompts/state-precision.md` in the local planning checkout) |
| M | [#18: Architecture experiment: compare compact liquid flow memory inline and in sidecars](https://github.com/techrote/cybersand/issues/18) | Compact motion (`architecture-programme-prompts/compact-motion.md` in the local planning checkout) |
| V | [#19: Architecture experiment: reconstruct fractional liquid interfaces without changing simulation](https://github.com/techrote/cybersand/issues/19) | Fractional presentation (`architecture-programme-prompts/fractional-presentation.md` in the local planning checkout) |
| B | [#20: Architecture experiment: gate and test bounded sparse ballistic material transfer](https://github.com/techrote/cybersand/issues/20) | Sparse motion (`architecture-programme-prompts/sparse-motion.md` in the local planning checkout) |
| G | [#14: Architecture decision: reconcile Cell, liquid and sparse-motion experiment evidence](https://github.com/techrote/cybersand/issues/14) | Decision review (`architecture-programme-prompts/decision-review.md` in the local planning checkout) |
| R | Existing [#12](https://github.com/techrote/cybersand/issues/12), reused | Soliding supplement (`architecture-programme-prompts/soliding-supplement.md` in the local planning checkout) |

Seven new boundaries are justified: two independent initial evidence questions,
precision before semantics, one compact-history question, independent presentation,
a separately gated sparse-motion proof, and the decision that consumes evidence.
Keeping ballistic and history distinct prevents a continuous-motion algorithm
from masquerading as state-layout cost. A decision issue is separate from code so
measurements do not silently adopt policy. Existing #12 prevents a duplicate
coherent-body backlog. D0–D5, general yield/reactions, registry expansion, torque,
fracture, anchors, rebaking and streaming are not automatically issued.

## Final quality and documentation gate

Review the ledger (`architecture-programme-source-ledger.md` in the local planning checkout) and every prompt for
the user's 30 requirements: full four-source trajectory; Current/proposal and
ADR/issue-local distinctions; occupancy/material separation; no external-source
reanalysis or mandatory ladder; independent width/packing/epoch/precision/solver;
independent geometry; characterizing both liquids; conservation and retained
physics policy; cross-dependencies, negative/ambiguous/no-go outcomes; master
before issues and overlap check; self-contained prompts; conditional downstream
work; bounded ownership/determinism; no production edits.

Documentation synchronization: programme owns only future research, with ledger
and prompts excluded from ordinary Current answers. Navigation, roadmap and
retrieval manifest route to it. Existing subsystem/ADR/runtime/evidence claims
are unchanged. Run documentation, historical M11, repository, frozen retrieval,
supplementary programme questions and diff checks; report inherited provenance
failures separately. No physics/runtime campaign is needed for this planning-only
change. Final issue readback, link/section/dependency checks and source-scope
inspection complete this task. The planning execution report (`../audits/2026-09-10-architecture-programme.md` in the local planning checkout)
records created issues, exact remote/dependency readback, manual quality review
and separate documentation/retrieval versus inherited publication-check outcomes.

issues.title: UI: Experiment Tower entry button retains Space focus and retriggers reset
issues.body:
## Problem

The root `Experiment Tower / F9` button created in `godot/scripts/main.gd::_ready()` retains the default keyboard focus. Entering the Tower by clicking that button leaves it focused. Pressing Space for the normal jetpack/navigation input can therefore activate the focused button again and call `tower_reset()`, matching the observed behavior where releasing/using Space unexpectedly resets the Experiment Tower.

The buttons created inside `CyberTowerPanel` already set `focus_mode = Control.FOCUS_NONE`, so this outer entry button is inconsistent with the rest of the lab controls.

## Minimal fix

After creating the root button in `_ready()`, set:

```gdscript
tower_button.focus_mode = Control.FOCUS_NONE
```

before connecting/adding it.

## Acceptance

- Clicking `Experiment Tower / F9` enters the Tower without leaving a keyboard-activatable control focused.
- Pressing/holding/releasing Space while in the Tower performs only the intended character/jetpack input and never re-invokes `tower_reset()`.
- F9 still invokes Tower reset/entry exactly once per non-echo key press.
- Existing Tower-panel buttons remain mouse-operable.
- Add a focused UI/input regression if practical.

## Context

Found while preparing the #19 H-gate human Water Feel evaluation. The attempted H run was from an older pre-#19 checkout, so no H result was recorded. This focus bug is independently present in current `main` and should be fixed before relying on long human-test sessions.

## MicroScenarios linkage — 2026-09-18

Issue #27/MS-000 generalizes the Experiment Tower / Water Feel Lab launcher and therefore treats this focus/input fix as hygiene that must be closed before the common launcher is complete. Keep this issue a minimal UI/input correction; no broader MicroScenarios implementation belongs here.

issues.title: MS-000: Extract deterministic MicroScenarios harness from Experiment Tower / Water Feel Lab
issues.body:
## Status and role

**Planned apparatus/refactor work. No new physics semantics are authorized by this issue.**

MicroScenarios are the common deterministic scenario layer for playable exploratory
worlds, human tuning apparatus, regression fixtures and benchmarks. This issue
extracts/generalizes capabilities already proven by #13 Experiment Tower and #19
Water Feel Lab rather than inventing another game architecture.

**Execution-order warning:** issue numbers are identifiers, not a serial path.
The canonical programme graph is
[`docs/operations/microscenarios-programme.md`](https://github.com/techrote/cybersand/blob/main/docs/operations/microscenarios-programme.md).
If this issue ever conflicts with that programme or the architecture programme,
reconcile the planning documents before changing implementation.

## Sequencing and dependencies

- **#18 is not a prerequisite.** #18 continues under its own compact-motion
  admission/acceptance contract. MS-000 must not alter its registered controls or
  become post-hoc evidence for/against flow history.
- Resolve #24's Tower input/focus defect before the common launcher is considered
  complete. Implementation may begin from a base that already contains that fix,
  or take it as an explicitly isolated prerequisite immediately before extraction.
- #20 may continue design/admission independently. Its implementation fixtures
  should consume the common harness once available, but #20 still requires
  #18/G-M plus its own G-B ownership/capacity/scientific admission.
- #26 is **not blocked** on MS-000. Continue source-matched characterization on
  existing apparatus when appropriate; re-express fixtures through MS-000 only
  when that does not invalidate registered evidence.
- #28 may begin exploratory/reference scenario authoring as soon as enough of
  MS-000 is stable to host it. **G-final is not a hard prerequisite for
  exploratory scenarios.**
- #29/INT-000 planning/inventory may occur in parallel. Its implementation needs
  a stable interaction-fixture contract plus the #28 Materials Laboratory
  readiness checkpoint.
- #14/G-final remains the independent architecture decision gate and is neither
  satisfied nor weakened by this apparatus.

Existing authorities to preserve: #13, #19,
`docs/operations/experiment-tower.md`, accepted ADRs, the current architecture
programme and the canonical MicroScenarios programme.

## Goal

Provide one small reusable scenario contract so the same definition can run as:

- **Play** — ordinary objective/tool interaction with minimal instrumentation;
- **Inspect** — pause/single-step, probes, overlays, captures and controlled
  parameter/seed changes;
- **Benchmark** — repeatable headless/instrumented execution with exported
  metrics and provenance.

A MicroScenario describes a situation and observation contract. It must not
reimplement material physics.

## Minimum scenario contract

Each scenario definition should declare, with versioned provenance:

- stable scenario ID + schema/recipe version;
- deterministic seed;
- initial world/material recipe;
- simulation/profile/config selections already legal at World creation/reset
  boundaries;
- optional player spawn and generic tools;
- setup/reset lifecycle;
- optional bounded scheduled starting events;
- requested observations/metrics;
- optional objective/failure conditions;
- result/export metadata including source/artifact/profile identity.

Prefer declarative data plus a small bounded host API over scenario-specific
scene scripts.

## Bounded host operations

The common host may provide generic operations equivalent to:

- create/reset a world from a recipe;
- spawn/paint initial material regions during setup;
- spawn allowed entities/tools through existing owner boundaries;
- schedule a bounded existing event;
- observe a declared region/material/metric/condition;
- mark objective complete/fail;
- capture snapshot/observation metadata;
- record benchmark metrics.

Generic triggers may observe conditions such as region material amount,
temperature, entity entry, electrical/config state where such state already
exists, or timer/tick expiry.

**Do not provide an unrestricted mid-play "write arbitrary cells every tick"
scripting escape hatch.** Scenario logic should observe and request normal engine
operations; material interactions remain authoritative in CyberSand.

## Discovery support

MS-000 must support the programme's exploration -> capture -> reduce -> triage ->
regression workflow without turning scenario code into a physics owner.

A useful capture should retain scenario/version/seed, source/runtime identity,
effective profiles/config and observations so an anomaly found organically in a
larger world can be reduced to the smallest reproducible fixture. Classification
comes after capture/reduction: a symptom may belong to kinetic/contact physics,
non-kinetic intermaterial interaction, product/state initialization or a
cross-system integration bug.

## Shared runtime

Generalize useful #13/#19 controls without duplicating them:

- scenario browser/launcher;
- fresh reset retaining only explicitly declared selection state;
- pause/resume and bounded single-step;
- deterministic seed selection where permitted;
- save/load or snapshot capture only within existing persistence/replay truthfulness;
- objective/status display for Play;
- optional dev overlays/metrics for Inspect/Benchmark;
- input/replay capture only to the extent current contracts support it;
- hide/minimize HUD for clean screenshots/video;
- export scenario ID/version, seed, effective profiles/config, source/runtime
  identity and observations.

Do not claim CYSD1 or current hashes provide complete replay when they do not.

## Initial migration/proving consumers

1. **Experiment Tower** — preserve shared recipe, floor/reset behavior, bounded
   command ownership, profile handling and historical chemistry-is-unchanged boundary.
2. **Water Feel Lab** — preserve deterministic scenario catalogue,
   transactional Apply + Reset, blind/reveal/export workflow and #17 correspondence.
3. Express at least one #26-style Water behavior fixture through the generic
   contract as proof the abstraction is not tied only to Tower UI.
4. Once #20 is independently admitted, express one #20-style bounded event
   fixture without changing #20's acceptance criteria.

## Non-goals

- No new Water solver, pressure field, velocity field, compact history,
  ballistics, chemistry/intermaterial retuning, new material catalogue, soliding
  semantics or Rapier authority.
- No rewrite of historical #13/#19 evidence.
- No requirement to make every legacy demo a MicroScenario immediately.
- No unbounded scripting VM/plugin system.
- No production save/replay redesign.
- No freezing of current imperfect physics merely so scenario content can exist.

## Acceptance criteria

- Existing #13/#19 reference scenarios retain source-matched behavior; expected
  metadata/schema differences are explicitly normalized rather than mislabeled
  as physics changes.
- Reset/owner/threading/failure-quarantine/interest-region contracts remain intact.
- Scenario definitions are deterministic under their declared seed/config where
  the underlying engine contract is deterministic.
- Play/Inspect/Benchmark use the same scenario definition.
- #24's Space/focus regression is resolved before the common launcher is complete.
- At least one Water/non-Tower proving fixture demonstrates that the API is not
  hard-coded to #19.
- Common instrumentation can be disabled without changing authoritative
  simulation behavior.
- Desktop native and supported native Web profiles are validated where migrated
  apparatus currently supports them; unavailable coverage is recorded, not inferred.
- Documentation identifies MicroScenarios as apparatus/exploration infrastructure,
  not an adopted physics architecture.
- The canonical programme/roadmap/retrieval routes and issue mirrors remain
  synchronized; no numeric issue-order assumption is introduced.

## Completion result

A small stable harness exists. It enables exploratory #28 content and later
generated interaction fixtures without creating separate mini-project
architectures. It does **not** itself authorize an architecture migration or
material retune.

issues.title: MS-001: Reference MicroScenario pack — Materials Laboratory, Flood Control, Simulation Stress Test
issues.body:
## Status and sequencing

**Planned exploratory/reference MicroScenario work. G-final is not a blanket
prerequisite.**

Dependencies:
- enough of #27/MS-000 must be stable to host real scenarios through the common
  Play / Inspect / Benchmark contract;
- #24 launcher/input hygiene must already be resolved as part of that host.

Issue numbers are identifiers, not a serial path. The canonical ordering and
revalidation rules live in
[`docs/operations/microscenarios-programme.md`](https://github.com/techrote/cybersand/blob/main/docs/operations/microscenarios-programme.md).

This issue deliberately allows **exploratory/provisional** scenarios before
#14/G-final. That is useful rather than accidental: playing interesting worlds
while the physics is still imperfect should expose unknown material/contact/
interaction edge cases. If later architecture or physics changes affect a
scenario, version-bump and revalidate/rebaseline it; do not rewrite old evidence
or pretend it was always run on the new engine.

## Goal

Ship three deliberately different scenarios against the same MS-000 contract:

1. **Materials Laboratory** — experimental/tuning apparatus.
2. **Flood-Control Puzzle** — playable emergent-physics objective.
3. **Simulation Stress Test** — benchmark/profiling apparatus.

The same scenario definitions must remain usable through Play / Inspect /
Benchmark modes.

## A. Materials Laboratory

Create a modular controlled environment with bays for representative material
experiments. Reuse the existing material catalogue and current interaction
semantics; this issue does not itself retune materials.

Core capabilities:

- reproducible dispensers/setup recipes for chosen materials;
- generic heater/cooler/igniter/fan/pump/brush/erase-style tools only where the
  engine already has or separately admits the underlying operation;
- inspection of material ID/state, temperature/other existing fields,
  activity/chunk status and declared metrics;
- quick fresh reset;
- named presets for representative interactions;
- snapshot/observation export with scenario/profile/source identity;
- load/display the same generated interaction definition that can run headlessly.

### Materials Laboratory readiness checkpoint

This checkpoint **unblocks #29/INT-000 implementation without waiting for all of
#28 to close**.

It is ready when at least one generic generated interaction fixture can:

1. load/reset from the same definition used headlessly;
2. expose its scenario/source/profile/material identities;
3. display the declared observations/results;
4. preserve existing owner/reset/threading boundaries;
5. A/B a baseline/candidate definition without silently mutating a live worker.

Flood Control and Simulation Stress Test may continue independently after this
checkpoint.

## B. Flood-Control Puzzle

Create a compact hydraulic/environmental scenario whose objective is expressed in
world terms rather than scripted solution branches.

Candidate objectives include:

- keep a generator/zone dry;
- maintain reservoir level bounds;
- route contaminated liquid away from a protected basin;
- prevent overflow for a declared duration.

Use ordinary materials/systems: gates, barriers, pumps/drains if already
available/admitted, porous/loose materials and terrain modification. Permit
multiple physically valid solutions.

This scenario is intentionally useful **during** physics development. Unexpected
support, bridging, erosion, clogging, phase/product or interaction behavior should
be capturable and reducible into smaller fixtures rather than patched with
scenario-specific rules.

## C. Simulation Stress Test

This is the canonical name.

Provide configurable deterministic bounded stress recipes for workloads such as:

- sustained Water flow/waterfall;
- large granular collapse/avalanche;
- long-lived smoke/gas column where supported;
- bounded repeated events/explosions;
- mixed-system "chaos" profile.

Expose registered controls for material spawn/setup rate, world/active region,
event rate/capacity and relevant scheduler/worker settings only through legal
configuration surfaces.

Collect useful available equivalents of:

- frame/tick and simulation time distributions;
- active cells/blocks/chunks and sleep/wake work;
- queue/capacity high-water marks;
- allocations where observable;
- worker utilization/work counts where available;
- cells/records/events processed;
- source/artifact/scenario/config identity.

Do not add unbounded work merely to make the benchmark spectacular.

## Exploratory -> stabilized lifecycle

Each scenario version is explicitly one of:

- **exploratory/provisional** — valid for discovery on its pinned source/profile;
- **stabilized/reference** — revalidated against the relevant accepted baseline
  and suitable for retained regression/showcase claims.

G-final or later physics changes may require targeted revalidation of affected
scenario versions. Unaffected observations keep their original scope.

When a world exposes an anomaly:

1. capture exact scenario/source/profile identity;
2. reduce to the smallest reproducible MicroScenario/fixture;
3. triage to kinetic/contact, non-kinetic intermaterial, state/phase or
   cross-system ownership;
4. fix/tune in the owning subsystem;
5. retain a regression;
6. return to the larger world.

## Shared authoring constraints

- Scenario content requests engine behavior; it never replaces it.
- No scenario-specific material kernels.
- Generic tools/systems needed by several scenarios belong in the framework or a
  separately admitted engine feature.
- Anything genuinely unique stays in the scenario package.
- Preserve deterministic setup and explicit source/sink accounting where relevant.
- Avoid bespoke logic that makes automated and interactive versions disagree.
- Scenario needs do not waive #18/#20/#14 architecture gates.
- Rework of provisional scenario content is expected and preferable to delaying
  useful discovery.

## Acceptance criteria

- All three scenarios load/reset through the same MicroScenario host/schema.
- Play, Inspect and Benchmark can run the same definitions without divergent physics.
- Materials Laboratory reaches and records the readiness checkpoint above.
- Flood Control has several physically distinct successful approaches produced by
  normal simulation interactions rather than authored solution flags.
- Simulation Stress Test has repeatable named profiles and emits comparable
  telemetry with explicit capacity/budget outcomes.
- Observer/instrumentation-off checks show no authoritative behavior change.
- Common APIs remain generic; no Water-, flood- or stress-specific hook is added
  to MS-000 merely to pass this issue.
- Current invariants, ownership, failure quarantine, bounded work and
  persistence/replay truthfulness remain intact.
- Provisional/stabilized status and source/profile identity are explicit.
- Documentation clearly separates exploratory discovery/showcase acceptance from
  production physics acceptance.

## Future work intentionally not included

Later showcase packs should be created only when their underlying systems are
useful to exercise: Destructible Shooting Range, Mining / Excavation Toy,
Sewer / Drainage Sandbox, Environmental Puzzle Room, Breach-and-Extract,
Utility-Tunnel Incident and Industrial Accident.

Post-merge review keeps #26 closed as a valid negative experiment for its exact

owns a bounded apparatus/evidence correction. #45 implementation/acceptance waits
for #49; MicroScenarios/INT-000 may continue independently and only affected

## Purpose

Track the CyberSand MicroScenarios + intermaterial-interactions programme.

> **Do not execute this programme by GitHub issue number.** Issue numbers are

> in [`docs/operations/microscenarios-programme.md`](https://github.com/techrote/cybersand/blob/main/docs/operations/microscenarios-programme.md).
> #30 is a tracker, not an execution prerequisite.

MicroScenarios are a thin scenario layer over the existing engine. One definition
should be usable as a playable exploratory world, human tuning environment,
regression fixture and benchmark where appropriate. Scenario logic defines
**situation, objective, controls and observations**; authoritative engine systems
determine what physically happens.

Their purpose is now explicitly twofold:

1. provide reusable scenario/test/showcase infrastructure;
2. expose unknown physics/material edge cases organically while development is
   still in progress, then capture/reduce/triage them into retained regressions.

```text
#24 Tower/launcher hygiene

#27 stable fixture contract + #28 Materials Lab readiness -------> #29 INT-000

```

After relevant architecture/physics changes, affected provisional scenarios and
interaction fixtures are revalidated/rebaselined. They do **not** need to wait to
exist until G-final.

## Hard boundaries

- #24 must be resolved before the common #27 launcher is complete.
- #27 no longer waits for #18 or G-final; it is apparatus/refactor only.
- #18 remains under its existing compact-motion scientific contract.
- #20 remains blocked by #18/G-M and its own G-B admission; #27 merely supplies
  reusable apparatus when available.
- #26 is complete Outcome B. #49 repairs/version-controls its successor Water
  apparatus; #45 implementation/acceptance waits for #49. This Water correction
  does not block independent #28/#29 work.
- #14/G-final remains the architecture programme's decision gate. #28/#29 are not

- The #28 **Materials Laboratory readiness checkpoint is satisfied** and #28 is complete; #29 consumed that gate in PR #55 after reconciling the historical preflight against current main.
- #29/INT-000 infrastructure is merged/closed through PR #55; later accepted tuning uses named rolling
  kinetic/contact baselines rather than a global "physics finished" gate.

## Discovery workflow

```text
play/explore
   -> capture exact anomaly + identities
   -> reduce to smallest reproducible fixture
   -> triage owner
        kinetic/contact
        intermaterial interaction
        product/state/phase
        cross-system integration
   -> bounded fix/tuning
   -> retain regression/evidence
   -> return to the larger world
```

Do not classify a symptom before reducing it. A case such as Lava creating Stone
and then appearing to sink through it may be support/contact, density/permeability,
state initialization, update ordering, a non-kinetic interaction rule or a
cross-system bug.

## Framework principle

A MicroScenario package declares:

- stable ID/version and deterministic seed;
- initial world/material recipe;
- legal config/profile selections;
- optional player spawn/tools;
- setup/reset and bounded scheduled events;
- observations/metrics;
- optional objective/failure conditions;
- result/export/provenance metadata.

One shared host exposes **Play / Inspect / Benchmark**. Avoid arbitrary per-tick
cell scripting that would replace material physics.

## First scenario pack

#28 proves the abstraction with three deliberately different scenarios:

1. **Materials Laboratory** — experimental/tuning apparatus and INT-000 front end.
2. **Flood-Control Puzzle** — playable emergent-physics world whose exploration
   should reveal unknown edge cases.
3. **Simulation Stress Test** — deterministic performance/workload profiles and
   telemetry.

Before G-final these may be explicitly **exploratory/provisional**. Stabilized
versions are revalidated against relevant later accepted baselines.

## INT-000: non-kinetic intermaterial interactions

#29 is renamed/reframed from CHEM-000.

Its scope is material/material behavior other than kinetic/material-motion physics:
reaction, combustion, thermal/phase consequences, dissolution/corrosion,
curing, electrical, catalytic/growth/special state interactions and explicit
products/byproducts.

Kinetic movement/support/bridging/bracing/erosion/collision remains in existing
physics owners. MicroScenarios can discover those problems but INT-000 must not
hide them behind compensating rules.

INT-000 uses:

- family/default interaction rules;
- per-material adjustments;
- sparse directed/symmetric pair overrides;
- context/state modifiers;
- independent interaction channels;
- a validated resolver/compiler to compact runtime lookup data;
- generated fixtures;
- baseline + versioned tuning overlays;
- provenance and a coverage ledger;
- an effective-matrix/workbench view without making a dense matrix the authored
  source of truth.

64 materials imply 4096 ordered pairs and 256 imply 65536, so the programme must
not require bespoke human-authored rules for every pair.

Do not create all of these as issues until their underlying systems are useful to
exercise.

### Focused physics/showcase scenarios
- **Destructible Shooting Range**
- **Mining / Excavation Toy**
- **Sewer / Drainage Sandbox**

### Emergent gameplay tests
- **Environmental Puzzle Room**
- **Breach-and-Extract**

### Integrated vertical slices
- **Utility-Tunnel Incident**
- **Industrial Accident**

Together with Materials Laboratory, Flood-Control Puzzle and Simulation Stress
Test, these remain the ten named showcase concepts.

A useful soft maturity progression is Shooting Range -> Mining -> Sewer, then
Environmental Puzzle Room -> Breach-and-Extract, then Utility-Tunnel Incident ->
Industrial Accident. This is not a replacement for real dependency checks.

quantified, but both admitted no-state local candidates failed their preregistered
survival screens.

This issue owns the next architecture question: **how should Water transmit bounded
head/pressure information through a deep connected body when the local same-row
destination cells are already full?**

## Evidence / dependency

Depends on completed #26 **and** the apparatus correction in #49.

Historical #26 establishes, within apparatus-v1 scope:

- medium and deep outlet reservoirs have the same early discharge under the Current
  solver;
- communicating pools retain a large head error;
- the historical three-compartment unequal-head fixture retains a large head error;
- both tested radius-2 local candidates fail their registered primary bulk/head gates.

Post-merge review qualifies the v1 settling/U-tube/performance metrics. In
particular, the old 2,670-tick settling value and old 24-cell "U-tube" value are
historical measurements, not the successor acceptance oracle.

Do not tune old thresholds, combine the rejected arms, or reinterpret #26 history.
Wait for #49's versioned metrics/fixtures and fresh Current-Water control before
freezing #45 numeric acceptance.

## Architecture question

Can CyberSand add a bounded, deterministic head/pressure-transmission mechanism
that distinguishes shallow/medium/deep hydraulic head and can drive equalization
through saturated connected passages, without turning Water into an unbounded
pressure/Navier-Stokes solver or conflating the question with directional flow
memory?

The key distinction exposed by #26 is that **local transfer strength is not enough
when every immediate destination is full**. A viable mechanism needs a bounded way
for pressure/head information to cross that saturated region and eventually create
capacity/lift on the lower-head side.

## Admission / design phase first

Before implementation, compare bounded architecture families such as:

- immutable per-tick/per-active-region derived column/head summaries;
- a bounded scalar pressure/head carrier with explicit lifetime and transfer
  semantics;
- staged local pressure propagation with fixed capacity/horizon;
- another source-backed bounded mechanism that can explain how saturated passages
  transmit head.

Do not select an implementation merely because it is easiest to code. Record:

- ownership and thread/scheduler interaction;
- read/write radius and race implications;
- storage/scratch/capacity cost;
- sleep/wake semantics;
- exact reset/failure behavior;
- whether the carrier is derived each tick or persistent;
- why it is **not** #18 directional momentum/history.

If every bounded design is worse than a larger explicitly admitted solver change,
record that no-go rather than smuggling in unbounded work.

## Required control

After #49 merges, use its **versioned corrected successor apparatus**, including:

- shallow/medium/deep identical outlets under the corrected metric schema;
- communicating pools with explicit expected wet coverage/equilibrium semantics;
- the new clean two-limb unequal-head fixture with roofed connecting passage and
  mass/geometry-derived equilibrium reference;
- constriction;
- fast dump;
- corrected calm-settling acceptance;
- ledge-sheet positive control;
- separated startup/active/sleep/total performance accounting;
- overwrite-safe, failure-retaining evidence output.

Retain exact source/artifact/profile identity. Keep all #26 apparatus-v1 results as
historical evidence and never rewrite them as if produced by #49's corrected
fixtures/metrics.

## Required outcomes

A candidate worthy of later human H review must, at minimum:

- create a measurable monotonic head response across shallow/medium/deep outlets;
- materially reduce the registered communicating-pool and unequal-head U-tube
  level differences rather than merely keeping them awake;
- improve calm-settling time without perpetual crawling/oscillation;
- preserve exact closed Water integer mass and source/sink ledgers;
- preserve deterministic expected worker parity;
- preserve bounded work/capacity with explicit saturation/failure outcomes;
- preserve protected granular/transport policies;
- keep ledge-sheet/shallow behavior acceptably lively;
- report p50/p95/p99/max/total cost and active/wake work.

Freeze numerical acceptance thresholds before candidate code using the fresh,
source-matched **#49 corrected Current-Water baseline** as the successor control.
Historical #26 values may inform context but cannot substitute for that baseline.

## Hard boundaries

This issue does **not** authorize:

- full Navier-Stokes or an unbounded/global pressure solve;
- universal cellular velocity or momentum state;
- #18 compact directional history;
- #20 sparse ballistic transfer;
- production Cell-layout migration;
- generalized liquid unification;
- weakening ADR-005 exact Water conservation;
- worker Godot/Rapier calls or mutable cross-owner state.

If the design needs a new persistent/derived carrier, state its ownership and ADR
impact explicitly before implementation.

## Programme ordering

- **#18 remains held** while this bulk head/leveling confound is unresolved.
  Direction-horizontal/diagonal evidence is not a clean stored-momentum oracle
  while a known saturated-head defect remains.
- #20 remains downstream of #18/G-M and its own G-B admission.
- #14/G-final remains open.
- #28/#29 MicroScenario work remains independent/provisional and may continue;
  affected Water scenarios are revalidated after any accepted change here.

## Completion

Complete with either:

1. a bounded candidate with source-matched automated evidence and focused owner H
   review sufficient to hand a new Water baseline to #18; or
2. a documented no-go showing why the admitted bounded families cannot meet the
   contract, with the next architecture decision stated explicitly.

A negative result is valid completion.

The original audit was claim-focused with targeted source verification, not exhaustive certification. This final audit must therefore also rescreen the repository for **new examples of the same failure classes** introduced after 2026-09-20.

At minimum search for:

- “complete”, “completed”, “accepted”, “ready”, “production”, “validated”, “all green”, “parity”, “runtime”, “Windows”, “browser”, “GPU”, “owner accepted”, “H-ready”, “performance win”, “faster”, “zero”, “no allocation”;
